taxonomic_note: Legacy Master Plant Pool name Chamaesyce fendleri is normalized to the current accepted Euphorbia name.
look_here_first: START WITH LOW, SMOOTH, AND ROUND. Fendler's sandmat (E. fendleri) is a small perennial with clustered prostrate to ascending GLABROUS stems from a woody thickened crown (woody root not photographed in any cleared public photo yet). Leaves are opposite, small, broad and rounded-to-ovate, with ENTIRE margins rather than the narrow linear blades of E. angusta. Look closely for glabrous 3-lobed green capsule and distinct linear stipules. True photographed detached seeds are pale and strongly FOUR-ANGLED, with slight wrinkles and occasional depressions, NOT regular prominent transverse seed ridges. Compare E. serpens (tiny annual mat with fused scale stipules) and E. angusta (erect, narrow, strigose leaves); cyathial gland appendage size and color are highly variable and should not lead the identification. Formal BONAP/NAPA native-by-county badge remains on hold.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays-local legacy Chamaesyce source; current Kew explicitly treats Chamaesyce fendleri as a synonym of Euphorbia fendleri.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Installed for active visual learning; broader exact-county reconciliation deferred.

morphology_keys.family_pattern: Euphorbia sect. Anisophyllum sandmat. Habit longevity, stipules, leaf margins, capsule surface, and seed form are more reliable than gland-appendage shape.
morphology_keys.growth_form: Perennial with woody, thickened taproot; stems usually prostrate, decumbent, or ascending, very rarely erect, densely clustered from the woody crown, about 5–12 cm.
morphology_keys.leaves: Usually opposite, rarely whorled; blades typically orbiculate to ovate, rarely almost lanceolate, about 3–8 × 2.5–7 mm; base slightly asymmetric and slightly cordate to rounded/obtuse; margins entire; surfaces glabrous.
morphology_keys.stipules: Distinct, narrowly linear, about 0.5–1 mm, glabrous.
morphology_keys.cyathium: Solitary at distal nodes. Four yellow-green to reddish glands; appendages absent or white/pink and highly variable in size/shape, so appendage form should not be used as a primary ID character.
morphology_keys.seed: Seeds white, ovoid-pyramidal, prominently 4-angled in cross section, about 1.7–2 × 1–1.2 mm, smooth to slightly wrinkled.
best_field_traits: dense cluster of very low glabrous stems
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Against the tiny annual sandmats, the woody perennial base is a major clue. Against E. angusta, E. fendleri stays low and has short rounded leaves; E. angusta is erect with very narrow distal leaves. Do not lean heavily on involucral gland appendage shape because it is variable in E. fendleri.

photo_note: Eight saved exact-species photos. FIVE photo files have individually traceable Commons CC BY-SA or CC BY-NC licensing for a genuinely noncommercial educational public learner, and all FIVE now have 14 manually verified structure annotations on actual saved source pixels (oval entire leaves, smooth stems, cyathial gland appendages, smooth three-lobed capsule with styles, dissected fruit versus true loose seed, four-angled pale seed and authored scale divisions). THREE UT Austin composite/voucher/stipule images lack explicit public-reuse clearance and remain withheld; historical internal descriptions may still refer to them. Woody perennial rooted crown still lacks a legally reusable photo; maturity of the isolated seeds is not certified.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: ROUND SMOOTH LEAVES + SMOOTH CAPSULE + FOUR-ANGLED SEED
steps: Find dense LOW sprawling or ascending stems with small opposite, broadly rounded-to-ovate leaf pairs; entire margins and smooth leaf surfaces should be visible.
Get a 10× close-up of one green fruit. Identify the smooth slightly flattened THREE-LOBED CAPSULE and its divided style arms; do not confuse the cyathium with a capsule.
At the leaf base, look for two SEPARATE narrow linear stipules (often 0.5–1 mm), not the broad fused scale seen in E. serpens; a public-license macro of the actual attachment is still needed.
Check loose seed versus opened fruit using the real photo panel; mature seeds are pale, 4-angled, and approximately 1.7–2 mm per FNA, but don't claim maturity from our source photographs.
Look for multiple shoots arising from a persistent thickened woody crown if disturbance or naturally exposed root-base allows; do not dig up a plant solely to teach this trait.
Compare against E. angusta (erect long thin pubescent leaves) and E. villifera (often hairy/papillate, different stipules); white gland appendage shape alone is not diagnostic.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: Only five of eight reference photo sources may display under the existing public educational license policy. UT Austin voucher and stipule close-ups are private/reference-only. The publicly available photographs do not demonstrate the living woody crown or isolate the 0.5–1mm separated stipule; maturity of pictured seeds not fully proved.
